html:
The global landscape is dominated by escalating US-Iran tensions, with the US military striking three Iranian oil tankers after its warships were reportedly targeted, while simultaneously, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow with a proposal from President Trump to end the war in Ukraine. This reflects a complex and potentially contradictory US foreign policy approach, balancing direct military action in one region with peace overtures in another.

US-Iran Conflict: The US launched strikes against three Iranian oil tankers, citing missile attacks on US Navy warships, further escalating tensions after weeks of relative calm. President Trump has warned of more strikes and threatened to hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, even appearing to downplay the conflict as "small potatoes" earlier. The US has also sanctioned a Turkish bank, Golden Global, identifying it as a "critical financial lifeline" for Iran, and senior US military staff are reportedly undergoing polygraph tests due to concerns over leaks regarding Iran. This rising friction is rattling markets, with GCC debt spreads hitting a five-year high, while the 'New York Times' reports Iran is more confident and capable after six months of conflict with Washington. The Ground Forces of the Revolutionary Guard also announced the dismantling of a cell linked to the occupation and Washington in Sistan and Baluchestan, and the US military may extend deployments in the Middle East until 2027.

Ukraine Diplomacy & War: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Moscow, met by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, carrying a proposal from President Trump to end the war in Ukraine. Both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy have reportedly ordered a halt to airstrikes for the visit, though Moscow has not publicly confirmed the cessation. Meanwhile, Russia has continued its intense bombardment of Ukraine, striking Kyiv's intelligence HQ and central Kyiv, raising questions about whether Putin is emboldened by the US focus on Iran.

Global Economic & Disaster Impacts: Global diesel prices have reached a record high. The devastating glacial floods in Nepal have crippled over 10% of the nation's hydropower capacity, raising questions about climate justice and prompting calls for international responsibility. Rescuers pulled a Chinese national alive from a Nepal tunnel 10 days after the flash flood, which has killed over 1,300 people. In Bolivia, at least two people died and dozens were injured in an explosion at a military barracks in Viacha, with authorities fearing the death toll will rise. Separately, Uber announced its immediate withdrawal from Nigeria and Uganda amid global restructuring and competition.

International Political Developments: The United Nations has adopted a new world map that more accurately reflects Africa's true size, a resolution sponsored by African states to counter perceptions of the continent's periphery, with the US standing alone in opposition. In UK politics, Reform UK leader Farage sought to address controversies at his party's conference, including allegations of evasions on overseas donations and the access given to an individual on bail for harassment charges. Black-clad protesters in balaclavas also blocked roads at the port of Dover. In the Philippines, Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail after an arrest order on charges she publicly threatened to arrange the assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., fueling a political showdown.

Security and Justice Concerns: A UN experts' report is urging an extension of a weapons embargo to the whole of Sudan, highlighting the responsibility of foreign entities in the ongoing three-year conflict. In Syria, a court sentenced former dictator Bashar Assad to death for crimes against his people, though many survivors are demanding more transitional justice. A Maltese businessman, Yorgen Fenech, was acquitted of complicity in the murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, nearly nine years after the attack, leaving the question of who ordered her death unanswered. The US ambassador also called for 'severe consequences' to stop West Bank violence, and Israeli forces have demolished Palestinian homes there.
